- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+ → 75+), then undercorrects, leading to persistent overprediction.
- Underestimates mean-reverting periods — model fails to recognize when prices are drifting toward historical averages.
- Lags in response to recent price movements; model reacts slowly to downward trends or sudden drops.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (10+ days) — exhibits asymmetric bias.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model fails to anticipate further acceleration; when downward, it underestimates the depth of decline.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — once a price spike occurs, it holds the forecast high for several days, even if true price starts to decline.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to capture volatility clustering or sudden reversals in price direction.
- In low-volatility periods, model underestimates the risk of sudden spikes or corrections.
- Model tends to overfit recent trends, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns.
